scope: Official documentation, local SDK and 52 catalog candidates; no authenticated requests in this audit.
data_constraint: All observations through BCCh API; INE documentation only for CPI publication schedule.

SearchSeries.date_semantics: Series-level metadata; dates may be absent or ND

unsupported_inferences: createdAt is first historical public release
statusCode OK means unrevised final value

catalog_vintages.scope_limit: Pattern audit, not exhaustive discovery of every versioning mechanism. Alternative base-year series are not automatically vintages.

sensitivity_contract.vintage_values: Latest retrieved values in all scenarios
sensitivity_contract.comparison: Same evaluation intersection, horizon and fitting procedure across lags
not_claims: Universal upper bound on publication delay

snapshot_comparison_contract.equal_snapshots_mean: Unchanged between these two retrievals only
snapshot_comparison_contract.changed_snapshots_mean: Change occurred within the retrieval interval; exact publication timestamp remains unknown

monetary_financial_monthly.rule: Current family policy: provisional release day 7 of following month or next business day; final version with lag of two months and 23 days; exceptional revisions possible.
monetary_financial_monthly.status: Current family rule, not historical release dates for every code

credit_survey_quarterly.rule: Release in January, April, July and October. Verified dates in 2026: January 14, April 15, July 15, October 14.
credit_survey_quarterly.status: Lag from quarter END, not encoded first day

expectations.rule: EEE released during survey month; EOF follows events around monetary policy meetings.
expectations.status: Calendar examples, not complete history or API ingestion timestamps

activity.rule: Official FAQ: 31 days after month end; August 2026 appears on October 1 calendar.
activity.status: Conservative month-end assumption based on current rule

prices.rule: September 2026 CPI published October 8 by INE.
prices.status: Producer release example, not BDE ingestion timestamp

derivatives_monthly.status: Family example; does not establish release time for each series or daily positions

unverified_by_code.status: No per-code historical release schedule reconstructed; use explicit 0/1/2 month sensitivity scenarios

target_common_constraints: Keep out of factor selection and weight optimization
Same survey and overlapping informants: not four independent replications
Demand strength may represent refinancing or liquidity need; not automatically greed

controls.not_independent_of: Real-credit predictors deflated by the same CPI

unit_cautions.issue: Nominal stock, billions of CLP, individual balance sheets; not flow or SME-only lending. Deflate before computing real growth.
Catalog unit Indice conflicts with related IEF percentage presentation. Exact code definition and consolidation mapping unresolved. Not percentage of borrowers.
Official metadata labels porcentaje de utilidad; do not assert multiples in times or fair-value thresholds.
Both millions of CLP; denominator is stock and numerator monthly flow. Ratio is not number of trades.
Gross banking spread, 30-89 days; not sovereign default spread.
Rates in percent; differences in percentage points, multiply by 100 for basis points. Compare matching nominal-real maturities.
Millions of USD; stock/flow, net/gross and counterparty orientation differ. No speculative sign established.
Catalog horizon is 11 months; alias12 is shorthand. Medians do not reveal dispersion.
Catalog horizon is 23 months; cannot directly subtract five-year inflation compensation.
TPM-incidence factor, not official financial conditions index; event frequency despite DAILY metadata.
Nested monetary aggregates/components; not independent votes; ratios do not uniquely identify risk appetite.
Consumption only, not all household or mortgage credit.
Balance is an algebraic function of five response shares; not independent validation of them.
Original linked series, 2018 reference; not seasonally adjusted.
General linked CPI from 2009-12; 12-month real credit growth starts no earlier than 2010-12.
